excerpt: The roads behind the Grand Strand's worst crashes, what federal crash data actually shows about seasonal risk, and your rights after a wreck.
keyTakeaways: The Grand Strand's roughly 18 million annual visitors help make Horry County one of South Carolina's highest-crash counties — 4th of 46 for total collisions and 3rd for fatal collisions in 2024. U.S. 17 carries more fatal crashes than any other Horry County route (67 between 2020 and 2024, per federal data counting every way officers recorded the route), and summer is not the deadliest season — 22.6% of fatal crashes fall in June through August, below an even spread. S.C. 9 at Highway 57 near Little River has had more crashes than any other Horry County intersection three years running (116 in 2024, per SCDPS). South Carolina's three-year statute of limitations (S.C. Code § 15-3-530) and comparative fault rule (less than 51% at fault) protect victims, including out-of-state tourists injured on Grand Strand roads.

faqs.question: Which road has the most fatal crashes in the Myrtle Beach area?
faqs.answer: U.S. 17 (Kings Highway) carries more fatal crashes than any other route in Horry County — 67 between 2020 and 2024, against 36 on U.S. 501, according to NHTSA federal crash data counting every way officers recorded each route. It is also the county's highest-crash road overall (1,821 collisions in 2024, SCDPS). Running through the heart of Myrtle Beach and the entire Grand Strand, it combines heavy tourist traffic, hundreds of commercial intersections, and frequent pedestrian crossings.

faqs.question: Which Myrtle Beach-area intersection has the most crashes?
faqs.answer: By state crash counts, it is S.C. 9 at Highway 57 near Little River — Horry County's highest-crash intersection in 2022, 2023 and 2024, with 116 collisions in 2024 (SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Book). U.S. 17 at S.C. 544 (78) and U.S. 501 at S.C. 544 (72) followed. U.S. 501 at Carolina Forest Boulevard was in the county's top five every year from 2020 to 2023. Most of these crashes are property-damage-only; none of the top intersections recorded a fatal collision in 2024.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident lawsuit in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Under S.C. Code § 15-3-530, you have three years from the date of your accident to file a personal injury lawsuit in South Carolina.

faqs.question: Are Myrtle Beach roads more dangerous in summer?
faqs.answer: Not for fatal crashes. Federal data for 2020–2024 shows 22.6% of Horry County's fatal crashes fell in June through August — below the 25% an even spread across the year would give, and below South Carolina's 26.1%. Summer brings far more traffic, unfamiliar drivers and pedestrian activity, but fatal crashes are spread across the calendar, with October, May and December the worst months.

faqs.question: Can I file a claim if I was a tourist injured in a Myrtle Beach car accident?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you are an out-of-state visitor injured in a Myrtle Beach car accident, you generally file your claim in South Carolina where the accident occurred. Your home state's uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage may also provide additional protection. An attorney experienced in cross-state claims can evaluate all available coverage options.

faqs.question: Can I still recover compensation if I was partially at fault for the crash?
faqs.answer: Yes. South Carolina follows a modified comparative fault rule that allows recovery as long as you are less than 51% at fault. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility.
